fictionLines.text: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Raj Warren is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
"Raj's gone." Asher looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Raj." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Ruby blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
📖 The Codex turns a page: Raj Warren, 42 days. The mantle passes to Ruby Callaghan.
🪞 You wake up somebody else. Ruby Callaghan, 24 — a lifeguard.
The village's quarrel was with Raj — and Raj is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
At the grave, Asher, Otis, Ntombi and 3 more speak for Ruby — "Raj trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
The fire knew Ruby before the Codex did — her name already carried weight here.

convoLines.text: "What's something you're good at that nobody here knows about?"
"Noted. Filing that under 'extremely useful.' The village needs that. I mean it."
"What's this about? I can do mending. Not well — well enough that nobody's died from it yet. That's my whole résumé now: nobody's died from it yet."
"Can I just — Still on what you're good at."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"You feel that? The air before a storm. That's the village right now."
You show them Lamb's Quarters — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"I tend the fire without being asked when the fire gets loud. Everyone's got a tell. That's mine."
"Anyway — I should get back to it. Good talking, though."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can I tell you something? I can't read, and I'm scared it matters now."
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
You walk to the ridge with Otis. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
"Don't tell anyone I told you. What's on your mind?"
"You want to know what I did in the raid? I stood down Drum-Belly at the treeline — it ran. Don't call it brave. Call it awake."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
"What's your first memory? Like, ever. The earliest thing."
"Three. That's young. The brain keeps what it needs, I guess."
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
"Mine's Columbus, Ohio, I think — heat on pavement, someone's hand huge around mine. Or I invented it. First memories are half real and half the story you needed."
"Still on your first memory."
"I don't know you well enough for that. Ask me again when we've survived something together."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You saw it too, right? Duel. Tell me I didn't imagine the lights."
"Moving! But — good talk! More later!"
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Got a read on anyone here yet? Who should I be watching?"
"Right, so — Same. But keep your eyes open — some people here are performing, not surviving."
"Watch the quiet ones. Not the loud — the loud tell you everything. The quiet are either thinking or planning, and you can't tell which until it matters."
"Still on your read on people here."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? Allegedly."
"Duel. They just... took Leo and Jordan. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
You show them Lamb's Quarters — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Ask me tomorrow. Everything changes by tomorrow."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"And... scene. Good talk."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"...Actually, forget it."
"It's quiet today. Wrong kind of quiet."
Maya has an edge today — something curdled.
They shake their head, then nod — both true at once. "Talk to me a bit. That helps more than anything."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
"Sorry — I got lost in it for a second. What did you want to ask? Good talking."
"I dreamed Sam was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."

"They're already drifting away. "Later."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"You'll never guess what I saw by the treeline."
"Saw things with too many joints. Give them room. That's the whole lesson."
They glance toward the fire, toward the others — checking who's listening.
"I — I don't remember saying that." A beat. "People hear what they want to hear."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"The treeline, this morning — something moved out there, big. By the time I looked properly it was gone. But I saw it."
